question_text: In the study of relations and functions, what is the 'domain' of a relation?
options: The set of all first coordinates (inputs) from the ordered pairs
The set of all second coordinates (outputs) from the ordered pairs
The graph plotted only on the positive y-axis
The rule that maps multiple outputs to a single input
correct_option: The set of all first coordinates (inputs) from the ordered pairs
explanation: As discussed in Unit 1: Relations and Functions (page 11), the domain of a relation consists of the set of all first coordinates of the ordered pairs.
subject: Mathematics
raw_source_snippet: Domain and range of a relation

question_text: Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for a relation to be classified as a function?
options: Every element in the domain is paired with exactly one element in the range
Every element in the range must be equal to zero
The relation must only contain negative integers
No two distinct inputs can produce the same output value
correct_option: Every element in the domain is paired with exactly one element in the range
explanation: Textbook definition (page 12): A function is a relation where each input in the domain maps to exactly one output in the range.
subject: Mathematics
raw_source_snippet: A relation is a function if each element in the domain is paired with exactly one element in the range.
